title: West Coast Airlines 956

location.name: Mt. Hood National Forest near Wemme, Oregon

summary: DC-9 Flight 956 descended below cleared altitude and struck terrain on eastern slope of Salmon Mountain during approach to Portland. Controller lost radar contact during right turn. Cause of descent below clearance never determined. Crew had limited DC-9 experience. Aircraft destroyed by impact and fire.
probable_cause: The Board determines the probable cause of this accident was the descent of the aircraft below its clearance limit and below that of surrounding obstructing terrain, but the Board has been unable to determine the cause of such descent. (p. 21)

factors.evidence: Captain Warren had over 18,900 flying hours but only 17 hours in DC-9 type (p. 19)
Aircraft flown on autopilot, descended normally to approximately 4,000 feet then leveled off (p. 21)
Controller lost radar contact with flight while in right turn (p. 21)
More than an hour after sunset, cloud ceiling at 2,900 feet with rain weather (p. 7)
Crashed October 1, 1966, approximately 5.5 miles south of Wemme on Salmon Mountain (p. 6)

events.text: Flight 956 departed Eugene for Portland, received IFR clearance via Victor Airway 23 at 12,000 feet (p. 6)
Flight proceeded toward Portland cruising at 12,000 feet without reported difficulty (p. 6)
Seattle Center at 2004:25 issued descent clearance to 9,000 feet. Crew acknowledged (p. 6)
Seattle Center about 1 minute later controller requested altitude, crew responded leaving 12,000 (p. 6)
Seattle Center issued vector turn right heading 300 degrees. Crew acknowledged but questioned direction of turn (p. 6-7)
Controller lost radar contact with flight during right turn while passing estimated heading 140-160 degrees (p. 7)
At 2009:09 crew requested to report when established on heading 300. At 2009:27 crew stated 'wilco' (p. 7)
When radar target failed to reappear, controller transmitted series of radio calls with no response. At 2015 accident notification initiated (p. 7)
Aircraft crashed on eastern slope at 45°51'21" W latitude, 121°59'36" W longitude in Mt. Hood National Forest (p. 7)
Ground witnesses in area reported seeing unusual orange glow near crash site. Aircraft sounded normal but appeared low (p. 7)
